items_missed: 1_set_agenda: never asked 'how are you today?'; no agenda statement (what we'll cover / how long it takes); no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation

2_probe: never got a full address or zip for origin or destination (only 'Comanche' as the destination town); didn't ask about stairs/floors at the destination; didn't ask about additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony); didn't ask about special considerations like narrow hallways or tight turns; didn't explicitly confirm packing needs or box count; didn't ask about access concerns (parking, HOA, elevator); never asked about moving stressors/worries
3_pricing: no 'pricing is super simple' opener; No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) never mentioned; Meet Your Mover email never mentioned; On-Time Guarantee never mentioned
4_clock: never explained the clock starts on-site when the contract opens; never mentioned the 2.5 hour minimum; never mentioned 15-minute prorated increments; no clock-specific sense-check

5_estimate: truck count never stated (movers count was); no stairs/elevator variable discussed; no walk-distance discussion; no equivalents used to frame the estimate; drive-time traffic not addressed
6_save_your_ass: entire prep speech missing -- no 'prep = shorter move = lower bill' framing, no consolidation examples, no carload tip, no close

7_quote_booking: never attempted to lock in the date on the call itself, deferred everything to a follow-up email/callback; 'no deposit required' never mentioned; didn't confirm a bolded key-details list at the top of the email; follow-up was framed as general callback, not as 'reply with any corrections'
9_bonus: no insurance explanation (No Worries + 60 cents/lb baseline) given despite handling several heavy/valuable items
top_strength: Dustin built real rapport in a call that could have stayed purely transactional -- when John shared that his wife passed away before Christmas, Dustin responded with a genuine, unscripted 'I'm sorry to hear about your wife, I definitely admire and respect that you're moving closer to your family and those grand babies,' and the forgetfulness banter ('I'm forty and also forgetful') kept the tone warm through the whole close.
coaching_note: You're strong on rapport and on itemizing inventory in detail, but the pricing pitch is missing its highest-value pieces: no No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, and no clock explanation (minimum, proration, when it starts). Those aren't optional extras -- they're what justifies the hourly rate and protects you if the move runs long. Also work the 'Save Your Ass' prep speech into every call; John has weeks before his move and consolidating loose items into a carload would have genuinely lowered his bill. Last thing: you had him engaged and ready -- ask to lock in one of the open dates on the call instead of only sending an email and hoping he calls back.
phone_presence_notes: Consistent warmth and natural affirmations ('Absolutely,' 'Yes sir,' genuine condolences on his wife's passing) kept John comfortable and talkative through a 29-minute call that ended on a clearly positive note.
